cdiDocs: Crew list
Minimum Safe Manning Certificate
Completed CDI Vessel Particulars Questionnaire (VPQ)
Completed officers' matrix from the CDI questionnaire
Continuous Synopsis Record
Certificate of Registry
Trading certificates (copies if originals ashore): Safety Equipment, Load Line, Safety Radio, IOPP, SAFCON, Tonnage, ISM DOC and SMC, COF/NLS, ISPS
Oil Record Book Parts I and II, and Cargo Record Book
Civil Liability for Oil Pollution (CLC 1992) certificates
USA Certificate of Financial Responsibility and last Tank Vessel Examination Letter / Letter of Compliance
Class certificate, ESP file with Condition Assessment Report, quarterly class reports and class survey reports
Approved manuals: stability, damage stability, inert gas, COW, CBT, ODME
SMPEP, SOPEP and OPA 90 manuals
SOLAS training manual, SOLAS maintenance manual, LSA/FFA maintenance records and fire training manual
Procedures and Arrangements (P&A) Manual
Cargo Gear Register
Officers' and crew national CoCs, proficiency certificates and dangerous cargo endorsements
Evidence of flag acceptance (endorsements) of crew CoCs
Manager's operating instructions
Company drug and alcohol policy and records of unannounced testing
Garbage Record Book and Garbage Management Plan
Ballast Water Management Plan
Mooring winch brake test records, rope/wire maker's certificates, bow stopper certificate; end-for-end dates as per the LMP
Last port State control inspection report
Hot work and enclosed space entry permits
Publications for the ship type listed in the CDI questionnaire
Records of work/rest hours
cdiPersonal: Rest hours during critical operations: C/O for tank cleaning, cargo start/stop/topping off and ODME; Master for manoeuvring; C/E for bunkering; all crew for drills and meetings
Hot work permits fully completed and closed, with office approval/closure emails
Checklists complete: bunkering, ship/shore safety, tank cleaning, pre-cargo, arrival and departure
Pre-cargo, bunkering and departure meetings recorded in the log book
Con handover between Master and duty officer logged
Watchkeeping levels logged
Drill entries in the log book up to date; avoid photos in drill reports (or use an intrinsically safe camera)
GMDSS annual battery test entry in the GMDSS log; Master signs the log daily
Battery room: PPE, eyewash, face shield, poster, ventilation warning, no leaks under batteries, emergency light working
BNWAS test records (primary and secondary buzzers)
Off-course alarm test records
ECDIS familiarisation checklist and joiners' familiarisation completed
C/O safety officer certificate
All navigation lights, mast lights and searchlights working
No alarms on the VDR; back-up procedure displayed and known to officers
All officers know gas meter calibration
O2 analyser calibration records for the VECS and the N2 generator
PV secondary venting alarm settings checked by the C/O
Sample locker arranged and segregated, ventilation working
Master aware of the worst damage stability condition
Cargo tank gauge calibration (empty tank and UTI comparison) and each temperature sensor calibrated
Correct shipping names (IBC Code / MEPC.2 circular), not commercial names, in the Cargo and Oil Record Books
Winch brake test records and certificates
Cargo gear and boat davit limit switches working
Fuel changeover records entered in the log book
Training manuals updated and in place
ER log books, bunkering plans, C/E's order book and standing orders checked
ORB Parts I and II entries for de-slopping
Master and C/E check due/overdue jobs in the company's SMS software
Coating Technical File available
Copy of the latest LOF form

drills.name: Emergency towing
drills.ref: ISM Code 8.1 (may be combined with the salvage drill)

drills.name: Recovery of persons from the water
Oil or NLS spill
drills.ref: MARPOL Annex I reg 37 and Annex II reg 17

drills.name: Release of LNG fuel
drills.ref: IGF Code reg 17 (not applicable to most oil/chemical tankers)

drills.name: Containment system failure
drills.ref: IGC Code 18.7.1 (not applicable to oil/chemical tankers)

drills.name: Other critical machinery failure
drills.ref: ISM Code 8.1 (may be covered by the emergency steering drill)

familiarisation: Do not sign every familiarisation item, including SMS reading, on the same date - keep to the 24-hour, 7-day and 30-day periods
ETO: add remarks for power generation, electrical/electronic equipment and all bridge alarms (no dedicated ETO page was a finding)
Give work familiarisation to catering staff too
Mooring familiarisation for all mooring crew, not only first-timers, especially where equipment differs (hydraulic brakes, mooring zone marking)
Engineers to complete the cargo watch items: CCR alarms, BWTS start/stop, IG/N2, power pack, VECS
Visitor/vendor familiarisation for superintendents, surveyors, vetting inspectors, terminal and cargo reps, bunker suppliers and chandlers
Visitor familiarisation records must match the gangway log
Visitors who sail with the ship complete both pages of the visitor familiarisation
When a group boards, brief everyone at the gangway, not only the vetting inspector
ECDIS familiarisation checklist should refer to the Nautical Institute 'Industry Recommendations for ECDIS Familiarisation'
restHours: Drill times shown as work hours
Alarm call-outs in the AMS (e.g. an oiler at 0300) shown in that person's work hours
Work hours match permit closure times
Bunkering: C/E's work starts 30 minutes before the barge comes alongside
Tank cleaning, cargo start/stop/topping off and ODME times reflected in work hours
Manoeuvring times shown as work hours
Safety and management meeting times shown as work hours
Person relieving the CCR duty officer for the SSSCL repeat check records the relief period
Rest hours cross-checked with the shipboard working arrangements
Senior deck officers' 2nd-level monitoring of cargo operations recorded
Chief cook and messman receiving provisions in off-duty time recorded
3 or more non-conformities for one person in 30 days is significant and leads to a SIRE observation
cyber: Shore training certificate on cyber security duties and responsibilities
Register/inventory of sensitive IT and OT systems
Procedure for admin and user profiles to access IT/OT
Procedure to check portable media before connecting to a computer
Records of approval to access IT/OT
Contact details of the IT person in charge
Contingency plan for a cyber attack
Active promotion of cyber security awareness
photos: Photos taken from height need a work-aloft permit, risk assessment and LOTO in place (e.g. crane winch limit switch, windlass from the forward mast)
Steering gear room general view should show the access
Deck photos should be close views rather than one general view from forward to aft
Remove the canvas cover from the emergency towing arrangement before photographing it
Photos must show the actual current condition on board
Photos must be representative of the area
Never use a photo from another (sister) vessel - it must show this ship's own equipment
